message.reasoning_content:
The user wants a block-breaking game (Breakout/Arkanoid). Language: Japanese. I want to build a single-file HTML game that feels crafted and alive — rich visuals, layered background, particles, screen shake, power-ups, combo system, level progression, sound via Web Audio, and a distinctive UI around it. Design instinct: the game itself should be the most characteristic thing on screen immediately, not a generic title card. So instead of a plain header, I'll frame the game in an arcade-cabinet-like layout with a side panel showing score, lives, level, combo, power-up legend. For type, I want a bold display face for the big numerals and title plus a readable body face. For a Japanese game, a chunky arcade display face works great — something like "Bungee" or "Rubik Mono One" or "Anton" — paired with "Zen Kaku Gothic New" or "M PLUS Rounded 1" for the Japanese body text. Let me use display: "Bungee" (blocky, arcade, literally block-like) and body: "Zen Kaku Gothic New" 700/500. Numerals: "Bungee" for score. Palette: I want an arcade CRT feel but not the tired near-black + single neon accent. Let me do a deep teal-navy base with warm amber/coral accents and multiple block hues (a full multi-color block palette). Background: layered — a dark slate-blue with a subtle scanline/grid, plus a soft radial glow, plus floating "brick" motifs drifting slowly. Add CRT scanline overlay lightly. Game features: - Canvas-based, responsive-ish, fixed logical resolution 960x640 with scaling. - Paddle with mouse/touch/keyboard control, ball with physics, brick grid with varying colors/HP, some indestructible bricks maybe. - Power-ups falling: expand paddle, multiball, slow ball, laser?, extra life, sticky. Keep a handful: 広げる (expand), 多球 (multiball), 減速 (slow), 残機+1, レーザー (laser). Laser adds complexity but fun — implement simple laser with spacebar. - Combo counter for consecutive brick hits without paddle touch → score multiplier. - Levels: 3-5 procedurally defined layouts, progressing. - Particles on brick break, screen shake, ball trail, paddle glow. - Sound: Web Audio synth blips (toggle mute). - HUD: score, high score (localStorage), level, lives as icons, combo meter. - Start overlay with instructions, pause (P/Esc), game over / clear screens. - Micro-interactions on side panel: hover on power-up legend chips, animated combo bar, buttons. For the surrounding layout, I'd rather do an asymmetric split than a stack of centered elements: left = big vertical title lockup rotated? Let's do: a top marquee bar (arcade cabinet marquee) with the logo left, status chips right; main area = canvas with cabinet bezel; right rail = score panel, combo meter, power-up legend, controls. Bottom strip = level progress / brick remaining bar. That's a rich, asymmetric layout. For the title, I'll avoid a gradient-painted headline; instead solid colors with a hard offset shadow — it reads more like a lit marquee sign. Let me write the code carefully. Canvas logical size: W=880, H=620. Scale via CSS width 100%, and handle DPR. Implementation details: Game state: ```js const state = { running:false, paused:false, over:false, level:1, score:0, lives:3, combo:0, comboTimer:0, best: localStorage } ``` Ball: {x,y,vx,vy,r, speed, stuck} Paddle: {x, w, h, targetW, laser, laserTime} Bricks: array of {x,y,w,h,alive,hp,color,points,type} Powerups: falling capsules {x,y,vy,type} Physics: substep collision to avoid tunneling. Use simple approach: move ball in small steps (e.g., split movement into steps of max 4px), check collisions with bricks via grid lookup or brute force over alive bricks (few hundred, fine at 60fps with substeps... 300 bricks * 8 substeps * 3 balls = 7200 checks/frame, fine). Brick collision resolution: AABB vs circle approximate — use closest point distance. Determine bounce axis by penetration overlap. Ball speed increases slightly per level and per N bricks broken. Level layouts: define as string maps with characters: '.' empty, digits 1-3 hp, 'X' indestructible (steel), 'S' stone? Let's use: - '.' empty - '1','2','3' hp - '#' steel (indestructible, just bounce) - 'P' guaranteed powerup brick Colors per row/level palette. Power-up types with weights: - 'M' multiball - 'E' expand paddle - 'S' slow ball - 'L' laser - '+1' life (rare) - 'C' shield/one-life-saver? Maybe 'G' glow ball (pierce). Let's add 'X' 貫通 (pierce ball) — fun. Keep 6 types. Effects timers: expand (12s), slow (10s), laser (10s). Laser: press Space while laser active → fire two bolts, cooldown 220ms. Combo: increments per brick destroyed; resets when ball hits paddle. Multiplier = 1 + floor(combo/5) capped at 5. Show combo meter with decaying bar? Simpler: combo resets on paddle hit; comboTimer not needed. But a decay timer adds life. I'll do: combo resets on paddle contact; also decays if no brick hit for 3s (bar shrinks). Screen shake: shakeMag decays. Particles: brick shards with velocity, gravity, fade; sparks on wall hits; paddle hit flash. Ball trail: store last N positions. Background inside canvas: dark gradient + faint grid + subtle vignette + drifting star/dust dots. Plus a "ghost bricks" pattern? Keep it: gradient + grid + moving diagonal light sweep. Sound: Web Audio API — small synth function: playTone(freq, dur, type, gain). Brick hit pitch rises with combo. Paddle thud, wall click, powerup arpeggio, life lost descending, level clear jingle. Input: mousemove over canvas → paddle x; touch; arrow keys / A-D; space to launch/fire; click to launch; P to pause; Enter to start/restart. Also "ball sticks to paddle at start" — launch with click/space. HUD in DOM (right rail) updated each frame: score with digit roll animation? Simple: update text, add a pop class on change. Level progress bar: bricks remaining / total. Also add a "next level" transition overlay drawn in DOM with animation. Let me also add cabinet details: bezel with corner bolts, marquee with title, side rail with vertical text "INSERT COIN" blinking, small "1CREDIT = 1 GAME" flavor. Scroll animations: page is mostly one screen; but include a section below with strategy tips / power-up cards that reveal on scroll via IntersectionObserver. I want to avoid a plain row of identical feature cards though — I'll present the power-up legend as a list with icons and hover, and below the game a "HOW TO PLAY" section in an asymmetric two-column layout with a numbered list and a keyboard diagram. Keep it moderate. Let me write the HTML/CSS/JS now. Fonts: Google Fonts — Bungee (display), Zen Kaku Gothic New (body JP). Maybe also "DotGothic16" for score numerals — dot matrix fits arcade! Use DotGothic16 for HUD numerals and small labels, Bungee for title, Zen Kaku Gothic New for body. Three faces is fine (display + JP body + mono-ish dot for numerals). Colors: - bg deep: #0d1b26 / #0a1620 (deep teal-navy) - panel: #12232f with border #1e3a4a - accent amber: #ffb648, coral: #ff5f56, mint: #46e0b0, sky: #4ec3ff - brick palette per level: coral, amber, mint, sky, plus violet #a98bff sparingly. The background is a deep teal-navy with a layered grid + glow, and the palette spans multiple hues (amber, coral, mint, sky) rather than leaning on one acid accent — it reads as a lit cabinet, not a minimal dark theme.
